title: Quire configured source
description: A user-supplied instantiation of a theme. Quire ships none of these: the repository contains no source URLs and no default catalogue (PLAN §1.3). The user adds each entry themselves, and is responsible for the legality of the sources they configure.

id.description: Stable local identifier. Never derived from the URL, so a source can be re-pointed without orphaning downloaded volumes.

name.description: Display name. Defaulted from the site <title> at probe time (PLAN §7.5 stage 6), then user-editable.

lang.description: BCP-47 language tag of the source's content.

theme.description: Registered theme ID that drives this source. 'generic' is the raw-selector escape hatch (PLAN §6 M2) and is the only value for which 'selectors' is permitted.

baseUrl.description: Site root, scheme included. http(s) only; enforced again at fetch time by the SSRF guard (PLAN §7.4).

overrides.description: Per-theme, schema-declared knobs. Each theme declares which keys it accepts and their defaults. PLAN §7.2: unknown keys are a validation error, not silently ignored -- so the permitted set is validated by the theme at load time, not here.

selectors.description: Raw selectors. ONLY valid when theme == 'generic'. Enforced by the allOf clause below.

script.description: Optional goja script hook. ONLY valid when theme == 'generic'. An escape hatch, not the main path (PLAN §6 M2).

allowedHosts.description: Extra hosts a redirect may land on. Absent this, the fetch layer rejects any redirect leaving baseUrl's registrable domain (PLAN §7.4). Image CDNs are the usual reason to set it. "example.test" matches that host and anything under it; "*.example.test" matches subdomains only. PLAN §7.5 stage 6 seeds this from the theme's own declared hosts, so it is usually already correct. It widens only the registrable-domain boundary: private, loopback and link-local addresses stay refused however they are named.

selfHosted.description: Present only when the user has confirmed this source is a service on their own network, which is what lets its host resolve into a private or CGNAT range that the fetch guard would otherwise refuse (PLAN §7.4). The guard refuses those ranges because scraped pages supply URLs Quire fetches unattended -- a cover URL is extracted from a listing and fetched with nobody watching -- so a hostile source can otherwise aim Quire at the user's own network; an unauthenticated /api/restart on a self-hosted service is the measured case. This exemption is scoped to this source's own host, matched exactly: no other host, no subdomain, no redirect target and no allowedHosts entry gets it, and content-supplied URLs pointing anywhere else stay refused. It is never inferred -- a probe, a theme or a redirect cannot produce it -- and a record without a usable confirmedAddr is a validation error rather than a flag that is quietly ignored.

confirmedAddr.description: The address the source's host resolved to when the user approved it, recorded so the entry shows what was agreed. Must be a private (RFC 1918 / ULA) or CGNAT (RFC 6598, where a tailnet lives) address: a public one needs no confirmation, and loopback, link-local and multicast are addresses no confirmation can cover. It is evidence, not a live check -- addresses on a home network move with a DHCP lease, and the host scoping is what does the constraining.

rateLimit.description: Per-source politeness. These narrow the global caps in PLAN §7.4 but can never widen them -- the fetch layer takes the stricter of the two, and the global floor is not configurable.

splitStrips.description: Vertical-scroll ('webtoon') strip splitting, PLAN §12.3. Tall single-image pages are cut into panel-shaped pages instead of being fitted into a 3:4 page as an unreadable centred sliver. Detection is per *image*, never per source -- a single index, and a single series, hosts both formats -- and it is biased hard toward doing nothing: a strip left unsplit is a sliver the reader can see, whereas a manga page wrongly split is mangled art across a whole volume, silently. 'auto' requires an aspect past the measured threshold (h:w 3.76, the empty middle between two stacked pages at 2.83 and the shortest real strip at 5.0) AND either corroboration from the rest of the chapter or a ratio past 10:1 that nothing else explains. 'never' disables it for this source. 'always' waives detection and hands every image to the splitter, which still leaves anything that already fits one page alone. This is an escape hatch: detection will eventually be wrong and the user should not have to wait for a release.

enabled.description: Per-source toggle surfaced in the source list (PLAN §6 M3).

lastProbe.description: Result of the most recent probe. Re-probed on failure (PLAN §6 M7) so a site that switched themes or added a challenge is reported as such, not as 'no results found'.

verdict.description: PLAN §7.5 verdict enum. 'blocked_challenge' is terminal: the source is refused, never added in a degraded state.

detail.description: Plain language, shown to the user as-is. PLAN §6 M3: a verdict is a complete final answer, not an error code and not a retry prompt.

themeScores.description: Fingerprint scores per theme from stage 4, kept so an 'unrecognised' verdict can name what was tried (PLAN §7.5).
